Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A typical angiosperm anther is bilobed, dithecous, and tetragonal, consisting of four microsporangia located at the corners.

Statement II: The innermost wall layer of a microsporangium is the tapetum, which nourishes the developing pollen grains.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A typical angiosperm stamen terminates in a bilobed anther, where each lobe contains two theca (dithecous) and two microsporangia.

Step 2: Evaluation
In transverse section, the anther appears four-sided (tetragonal) with four microsporangia at the corners, two in each lobe. Surrounding each microsporangium are four wall layers: epidermis, endothecium, middle layers, and the innermost tapetum, whose dense-cytoplasmic, often multinucleate cells nourish the developing pollen grains.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct because the anther is bilobed, dithecous, and tetragonal with four microsporangia, and the tapetum forms the innermost nutritive wall layer.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_STMT2_Q02 - Pollen grain exine and intine layers

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Pollen grains are well-preserved as fossils because their hard outer layer (exine) is made up of sporopollenin.

Statement II: The inner wall of the pollen grain (intine) is made up of sporopollenin and contains prominent apertures called germ pores.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A pollen grain has a two-layered wall consisting of an outer exine and an inner intine, each with distinct chemical composition.

Step 2: Evaluation
The exine is composed of sporopollenin, one of the most resistant organic materials known, which accounts for fossil preservation of pollen grains; germ pores are apertures in the exine where sporopollenin is absent. In contrast, the intine is a thin, continuous inner layer made up of cellulose and pectin, not sporopollenin.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim regarding sporopollenin in the exine enabling fossil preservation is correct, whereas the claim describing the intine as composed of sporopollenin with germ pores is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In over 60 per cent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at the 3-celled stage.

Statement II: In species that shed pollen at the 3-celled stage, the generative cell divides mitotically to give rise to two male gametes before shedding.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Mature pollen grains contain a vegetative cell and a generative cell, and are shed either at the 2-celled or 3-celled stage depending on the species.

Step 2: Evaluation
In over 60 per cent of angiosperms, pollen grains are shed at the 2-celled stage (one vegetative cell and one generative cell), not the 3-celled stage. In the remaining species, the generative cell divides mitotically to produce two male gametes before shedding, resulting in the 3-celled stage.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim that over 60 per cent of angiosperms shed pollen at the 3-celled stage is incorrect, whereas the claim explaining mitotic division of the generative cell prior to 3-celled shedding is correct.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_STMT2_Q04 - Pollen viability across cereals and dicot families

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In cereals such as rice and wheat, pollen grains maintain viability for several months after release.

Statement II: In members of Rosaceae, Leguminosae, and Solanaceae, pollen grains lose viability within 30 minutes of their release.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The period for which pollen grains remain viable varies widely across plant species.

Step 2: Evaluation
In cereals such as rice and wheat, pollen grains lose viability rapidly—within 30 minutes of their release—not after several months. Conversely, in some members of Rosaceae, Leguminosae, and Solanaceae, pollen grains maintain viability for months, not merely 30 minutes.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect because the viability durations for rice/wheat and Rosaceae/Leguminosae/Solanaceae are reversed.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_STMT2_Q05 - Gynoecium types and ovule number per ovary

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The gynoecium of Papaver is multicarpellary and syncarpous, whereas that of Michelia is multicarpellary and apocarpous.

Statement II: The number of ovules in an ovary may be one, as in wheat, paddy, and mango, or many, as in papaya, water melon, and orchids.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A multicarpellary gynoecium may have fused pistils (syncarpous) or free pistils (apocarpous), and ovaries differ in the number of ovules they enclose.

Step 2: Evaluation
Papaver has a multicarpellary, syncarpous pistil, while Michelia has a multicarpellary, apocarpous gynoecium. Furthermore, wheat, paddy, and mango contain a single ovule per ovary, whereas papaya, water melon, and orchids contain many ovules per ovary.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct because both the gynoecium classifications and the ovule-number examples match angiosperm morphology.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_STMT2_Q06 - Hilum, micropyle, and chalaza of an ovule

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In an angiosperm ovule, the hilum represents the junction between the body of the ovule and the funicle.

Statement II: The chalaza is a small opening organised at the tip of the integuments where they do not encircle the nucellus.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
An ovule is attached to the placenta by the funicle and surrounded by integuments that leave a small apical opening.

Step 2: Evaluation
The body of the ovule fuses with the funicle at the hilum, making the hilum the junction between the ovule and funicle. However, the small opening at the tip of the integuments is the micropyle, whereas the chalaza is the basal part of the ovule opposite the micropylar end.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The description of the hilum as the junction between ovule and funicle is correct, whereas identifying the micropylar opening as the chalaza is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a majority of flowering plants, all four megaspores formed from the megaspore mother cell remain functional and jointly form a single embryo sac.

Statement II: During embryo sac formation from the functional megaspore, the mitotic nuclear divisions up to the 8-nucleate stage are strictly free-nuclear.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Female gametophyte development in most angiosperms is monosporic and involves free-nuclear mitotic divisions.

Step 2: Evaluation
Out of the four megaspores produced by meiosis of the megaspore mother cell, only one is functional while the other three degenerate; thus, the claim that all four remain functional is incorrect. The nucleus of the single functional megaspore undergoes three sequential free-nuclear mitotic divisions (without immediate cell wall formation) to reach the 8-nucleate stage, making the second claim correct.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim that all four megaspores jointly form the embryo sac is incorrect, whereas the claim regarding strictly free-nuclear mitotic divisions up to the 8-nucleate stage is correct.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_STMT2_Q08 - Organisation of mature embryo sac and filiform apparatus

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A typical mature angiosperm embryo sac is 8-celled and 7-nucleate.

Statement II: The filiform apparatus consists of cellular thickenings at the chalazal tip of the antipodals that guide the pollen tube.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A mature angiosperm embryo sac has a characteristic distribution of nuclei and cells between the micropylar and chalazal poles.

Step 2: Evaluation
A mature embryo sac is 7-celled (3 cells in the egg apparatus, 3 antipodals, and 1 large central cell) and 8-nucleate (since the central cell contains 2 polar nuclei), so describing it as 8-celled and 7-nucleate is incorrect. Furthermore, the filiform apparatus is located at the micropylar tip of the synergids—not at the chalazal tip of the antipodals—to guide the pollen tube into a synergid.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect because the mature embryo sac is 7-celled and 8-nucleate, and the filiform apparatus is present on the synergids at the micropylar end.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Cleistogamous flowers do not open at all and are invariably autogamous, producing assured seed-set even in the absence of pollinators.

Statement II: Geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination involving a pollinating agent, but genetically it is similar to autogamy since the pollen grains come from the same plant.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Pollination types are classified based on the source of pollen and whether flowers open to expose reproductive organs.

Step 2: Evaluation
Cleistogamous flowers (as in Viola, Oxalis, and Commelina) never open, so anthers dehisce close to the stigma inside the bud, ensuring autogamy and assured seed-set without pollinators. Geitonogamy transfers pollen between two different flowers on the same plant, requiring a pollinating agent (functionally cross-pollination) while transferring genetically identical pollen from the same plant (genetically autogamy).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct as they accurately describe cleistogamy and geitonogamy.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_STMT2_Q10 - Pollination in Vallisneria versus water hyacinth

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Vallisneria, the female flower reaches the surface of water by a long stalk and pollen grains are carried passively by water currents on the surface.

Statement II: In water hyacinth and water lily, pollination takes place underwater through submerged ribbon-like pollen grains.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Aquatic angiosperms exhibit diverse pollination modes; not all aquatic plants are pollinated by water.

Step 2: Evaluation
In Vallisneria, the female flower reaches the water surface via a long stalk and male flowers/pollen grains released onto the surface are carried passively by water currents. However, in water hyacinth and water lily, the flowers emerge above the water level and are pollinated by insects or wind, not by submerged ribbon-like pollen (which is characteristic of marine seagrasses like Zostera).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The description of surface water pollination in Vallisneria is correct, whereas the claim that water hyacinth and water lily are pollinated underwater by ribbon-like pollen is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Both wind-pollinated and water-pollinated flowers are generally very colourful and produce abundant nectar.

Statement II: To compensate for uncertainties and associated loss of pollen grains, wind- and water-pollinated flowers produce an enormous amount of pollen compared to the number of ovules available.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Abiotic pollination (by wind or water) relies on chance contact between pollen and stigma rather than animal attraction.

Step 2: Evaluation
Wind- and water-pollinated flowers do not need to attract animal pollinators, so they are not very colourful and do not produce nectar; hence, claiming they are colourful and nectar-rich is incorrect. Because pollen contact with the stigma is a chance factor in both wind and water pollination, these flowers produce enormous amounts of pollen relative to ovule number to compensate for pollen loss.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim that abiotic-pollinated flowers are colourful and produce nectar is incorrect, whereas the claim regarding enormous pollen production to compensate for pollen loss is correct.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_STMT2_Q12 - Monoecy vs dioecy as outbreeding devices

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Production of unisexual flowers on the same plant (monoecy), as in castor and maize, prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy.

Statement II: Presence of male and female flowers on different plants (dioecy), as in papaya, prevents autogamy but cannot prevent geitonogamy.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Unisexual flowers prevent self-pollination within a flower, but their effect on geitonogamy depends on whether male and female flowers occur on the same plant or on separate plants.

Step 2: Evaluation
In monoecious plants (castor, maize), both male and female flowers are on the same plant, which prevents autogamy but does not prevent geitonogamy. In dioecious plants (papaya), each plant is either male or female, which prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect because monoecy prevents only autogamy (not geitonogamy), while dioecy prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_STMT2_Q13 - Emasculation necessity and pollen-pistil chemical dialogue

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In artificial hybridisation, emasculation is necessary if the female parent bears bisexual flowers, whereas it is not needed if the female parent produces unisexual flowers.

Statement II: The ability of the pistil to recognise compatible or incompatible pollen is the result of a continuous dialogue mediated by chemical components of the pollen and the pistil.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Artificial hybridisation prevents unwanted pollen contamination through emasculation and bagging, while natural pollen-pistil interaction relies on chemical recognition.

Step 2: Evaluation
When a female parent bears bisexual flowers, anthers must be removed before dehiscence (emasculation) to prevent self-pollination; unisexual female flowers lack anthers, making emasculation unnecessary. Furthermore, pollen recognition leading to acceptance or rejection by the pistil is mediated by chemical components of the pollen interacting with those of the pistil.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct as they accurately reflect artificial hybridisation protocols and pollen-pistil recognition.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_STMT2_Q14 - Double fertilisation products and tender coconut endosperm

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Double fertilisation involves syngamy to form a diploid zygote and triple fusion to form a triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN).

Statement II: In tender coconut, the coconut water represents the cellular endosperm while the surrounding white kernel represents the free-nuclear endosperm.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Double fertilisation produces a diploid zygote and a triploid primary endosperm nucleus, which subsequently develops into endosperm.

Step 2: Evaluation
Syngamy fuses one male gamete with the egg cell to form a diploid zygote, and triple fusion fuses the other male gamete with two polar nuclei to form a triploid PEN. However, in tender coconut, the liquid coconut water is the free-nuclear endosperm (thousands of free nuclei), while the surrounding white kernel is the cellular endosperm.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The description of double fertilisation products is correct, whereas the identification of coconut water as cellular endosperm and the white kernel as free-nuclear endosperm is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In a monocotyledonous grass embryo, the radicle and root cap are enclosed in a hollow foliar structure called the coleoptile.

Statement II: In a typical dicotyledonous embryo, the portion of the embryonal axis above the level of cotyledons is the epicotyl, which terminates with the plumule.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Embryos of monocots and dicots differ in cotyledon number and protective sheaths around the shoot and root apices.

Step 2: Evaluation
In a grass embryo, the radicle and root cap are enclosed in an undifferentiated sheath called the coleorrhiza, whereas the coleoptile is the hollow foliar structure enclosing the shoot apex and leaf primordia; thus, attributing the coleoptile to the radicle and root cap is incorrect. In a dicot embryo, the portion of the embryonal axis above the cotyledons is indeed the epicotyl, terminating in the plumule.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim that the coleoptile encloses the radicle and root cap is incorrect, whereas the description of the dicot epicotyl terminating in the plumule is correct.

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_SEXUALREPRODUCTIONINFLOWERINGPLANTS_STMT2_Q16 - Parthenocarpy vs apomixis in crop plants

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Parthenocarpic fruits such as banana develop after double fertilisation and always contain numerous viable seeds.

Statement II: Converting hybrid crop varieties into apomicts causes segregation of hybrid characters in the progeny, forcing farmers to buy new hybrid seeds every year.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Parthenocarpy is fruit development without fertilisation, while apomixis is seed formation without fertilisation.

Step 2: Evaluation
Parthenocarpic fruits such as banana develop without fertilisation and are seedless, making the claim that they form after double fertilisation with numerous seeds incorrect. Furthermore, converting hybrids into apomicts prevents segregation of hybrid characters in the progeny, allowing farmers to reuse hybrid seeds year after year rather than forcing them to buy new seeds annually.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect because parthenocarpic fruits are seedless and form without fertilisation, and apomixis prevents segregation in hybrid progeny.

Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
